Every regulated create, modify, correct, approve, verify, release, reject, hold, resume, disposition, quality-state change and integration write shall enter through the GxP Mutation Gateway. Frappe generic CRUD, direct DB writes, background scripts and adapters shall not create authoritative GxP state.
acceptance_intent: Architectural tests prove no supported bypass path.

required_behavior: Resolve human, service, integration or device identity from trusted server-side authentication context. Ignore client-supplied actor IDs/names for authority decisions.
acceptance_intent: Spoofed actor fields do not change attribution.

required_behavior: Resolve customer, legal entity, site and resource scope before business validation. Requests crossing tenant/site boundaries fail closed.
Each mutation uses a versioned command type such as CompleteBatchStep, CorrectResult, ApproveDeviation, ReleaseBatch, UpdateMaterialStatus or AcceptLIMSResult.
Validate command envelope and payload against versioned JSON Schema/OpenAPI contract before domain processing.
Call Policy/Authorization Service using subject, role, site, qualifications, resource state, requested action and SoD context.
acceptance_intent: Every regulated command has explicit allow/deny evidence.

required_behavior: Where configured, confirm required current training, equipment qualification, area qualification or task competency before allowing action.
Validate requested command against authoritative current state and allowed transition table; UI state is never authoritative.
Require expected aggregate/record version for mutations. Reject stale commands using optimistic concurrency.
acceptance_intent: Two simultaneous conflicting writes cannot silently overwrite.

required_behavior: Require idempotency key for commands capable of duplicate submission. Persist key, actor/source, command hash and resulting receipt.
acceptance_intent: Retries return same result without duplicate regulated event.

required_behavior: Rules identify commands requiring controlled reason/comment. Reason is structured, required before commit and preserved in audit.
acceptance_intent: Correction/override cannot proceed without required reason.

required_behavior: Determine whether electronic signature is required, signature meaning, required signer class and whether one or multiple signatures are required.
acceptance_intent: Signature need cannot be bypassed by client.

required_behavior: If signature is required, produce/consume a challenge bound to command, record ID, expected version/hash, meaning and expiry. Commit only after valid signature proof.
Execute applicable released rule/calculation versions for materials, equipment, limits, eligibility, sequence, QMS and release controls.
acceptance_intent: Rule result and version are persisted.

required_behavior: Persist domain state, new version, audit event and outbox message in one PostgreSQL transaction.
acceptance_intent: No state can commit without its audit/outbox companion.

required_behavior: Create audit record with actor, UTC time, source, action, old/new representation or references, reason, signature, correlation and rule/software versions.
acceptance_intent: Each committed mutation has auditable event.

required_behavior: Canonicalize resulting regulated record/version and calculate cryptographic digest where the record class requires integrity binding.
Write integration/domain event into outbox in the same transaction; external bus publishing occurs only after commit.
acceptance_intent: Bus outage cannot lose committed event.

required_behavior: Return immutable identifiers: command ID, aggregate ID, resulting version, audit event ID, signature ID if applicable, correlation ID and record hash where applicable.
Frappe projection/read model updates occur asynchronously after authoritative commit and may be retried without altering regulatory truth.
acceptance_intent: Projection failure does not roll back valid GxP commit.

required_behavior: Return stable machine-readable error codes for authentication, authorization, stale version, state violation, missing signature, rule failure, validation, dependency unavailable and system fault.
acceptance_intent: Clients do not depend on free-text errors.

required_behavior: If authoritative DB, Signature Service for required signings, Policy Service or integrity-critical component is unavailable, mutation does not succeed.
ERP/LIMS/Edge commands use non-human identities with narrowly scoped permissions and source-system IDs.
acceptance_intent: Integration cannot impersonate a human signer.

required_behavior: For machine-originated mutations/evidence, verify registered source/device identity and mapping before acceptance.
Detect timestamp/sequence anomalies and duplicate/replayed integration/device commands using source event IDs, sequences and idempotency.
Exceptional admin/data-repair actions require dedicated privileged command types, incident/change/deviation reference, stronger authorization and independent review.
Every command and generated event carries request, correlation and causation identifiers across services and adapters.
Retain sufficient command/receipt metadata for investigation, duplicate detection and validation evidence according to record class.
Command handlers shall call validated domain services; customer-provided Python/JavaScript is prohibited in authoritative mutation execution.
Command handlers explicitly support/deprecate schema versions; semantic changes require new version and migration/compatibility assessment.
acceptance_intent: Existing validated clients do not silently change behavior.

required_behavior: Repeated denied, replayed, malformed, privilege-escalation or suspicious mutations generate security monitoring events separate from GxP audit where appropriate.
Provide query by command ID/correlation ID/record to trace command → decision → signature → version → audit → outbox.
Every electronic signature is linked to one immutable individual subject identifier. Display names may change historically, but signer subject cannot be reassigned.
acceptance_intent: Historical signature remains attributable after rename/deactivation.

required_behavior: Customer organization must have a controlled process to verify identity before granting electronic-signature authority; system stores status/evidence reference where configured.
acceptance_intent: Unverified identity cannot receive signing entitlement.

required_behavior: Controlled meanings include Performed, Verified, Reviewed, Approved, Released, Rejected, Authored, Witnessed and customer-approved extensions.
acceptance_intent: Meaning is explicit in challenge, record and export.

required_behavior: Record/action policy defines required meaning, signer role/qualification, number/order of signatures, independent signer restrictions and authentication assurance.
acceptance_intent: Client cannot alter required signer policy.

required_behavior: Create server-side unique signature challenge containing challenge ID, signer subject, tenant/site, record ID, version/hash, action/meaning, nonce and expiry.
Every regulated Part 11 signature in V1 requires fresh step-up authentication through configured IdP; normal existing session alone is insufficient.
acceptance_intent: Recorded authentication time/assurance meets configured policy.

required_behavior: Non-biometric signature configuration must be validated to meet applicable §11.200 component controls. IdP policy must not silently downgrade required factors/components.
Although Part 11 distinguishes continuous sessions, V1 intentionally applies fresh step-up for every regulated signature as a stronger product baseline.
Persist trusted IdP issuer, subject, authentication time, method/AMR, assurance/ACR where available, session reference and challenge reference.
Signature binds exact regulated record ID, version and cryptographic hash (or canonical immutable snapshot ID).
Signature also binds intended action and meaning; an approval signature cannot be reused for release or correction.
Nonce/challenge is single use. Repeated callback/token cannot create second signature.
Expired challenge cannot be completed; new challenge requires re-evaluation against current record state/version.
If record or command-relevant state changes after challenge creation, signature challenge is invalidated.
Signed record and human-readable export show printed name, execution date/time and signature meaning.
Signature record is linked by immutable identifiers/hash so it cannot be excised, copied or transferred to another record by ordinary application means.
acceptance_intent: Copying signature ID to another record fails integrity checks.

required_behavior: Support performer/verifier, author/approver, QA reviewer/releaser and other ordered or independent signature chains.
Policy may require signer != performer/author/previous signer; signer role and qualification checked at signature completion time.
Failed step-up, expired challenge, wrong identity, denied policy and replay attempts do not create valid signature; security-relevant attempts are logged.
acceptance_intent: No orphan valid signature on failure.

required_behavior: Disabling signer prevents future signatures but does not invalidate historical legitimate signatures.
Identity credential recovery is handled by IdP policy; product does not expose old credentials. High-risk recovery may suspend signing until customer process completes.
Users cannot delegate their electronic signature. Workflow delegation may reassign work but new assignee signs as self.
Service/integration/device identity cannot create human Part 11 signature.
acceptance_intent: Service token rejected on human signature endpoint.

required_behavior: Architecture may accept customer IdP biometric/WebAuthn assurance later, but the GxP Signature Service still creates the regulatory signature record.
acceptance_intent: Authentication technology does not replace GxP record.

required_behavior: Signature execution time is assigned server-side in UTC; local timezone is presentation metadata.
acceptance_intent: Browser clock manipulation has no effect.

required_behavior: UI clearly displays what is being signed, meaning, relevant record identity/version and any required statement before step-up.
acceptance_intent: User cannot sign ambiguous hidden target.

required_behavior: Return signature_id, challenge_id, signer subject/name, time, meaning, record/version/hash and auth context reference.
acceptance_intent: Downstream transaction can reference exact signature.

required_behavior: A historical signature is never deleted. If signed record is superseded/corrected, old signature remains on old version; new version requires required new signatures.
Provide configurable evidence/report supporting customer's §11.100 certification/governance responsibilities; software does not submit certification automatically unless separately designed.
Authorized auditor can list all signatures for record/batch/user/time range and export manifestation plus linkage/integrity metadata.
GxP audit is a dedicated authoritative ledger separate from Frappe Version, application logs, Temporal history and SIEM logs.
acceptance_intent: Removing Frappe history does not remove GxP audit.

required_behavior: Committed regulated mutations automatically generate audit events; users cannot choose whether an applicable event is audited.
Each event receives authoritative server UTC time plus source/device timestamp metadata where relevant.
Record human/service/device actor type, immutable subject/source ID and display/context metadata.
Use stable event types: Created, Changed, Corrected, Signed, Approved, Released, StatusChanged, Consumed, Returned, IntegrationAccepted, etc.
For changed regulated data preserve old and new values or immutable version references sufficient to reconstruct the change.
Record normalized changed fields for review/search without relying only on full JSON diff.
acceptance_intent: QA can filter changed critical parameters.

required_behavior: Store mandatory reason/comment for controlled correction, override, manual replacement, admin repair and other policy-defined changes.
Audit event references signature ID(s) and meaning where action is signed.
Every event references aggregate/record and resulting version; where applicable record digest.
Persist request/correlation/causation IDs to connect UI command, background activity and integration side effects.
Identify Frappe UI, REST API, ERP, LIMS, Edge, background system, migration or privileged repair source.
Record product release and critical rule/calculation version used for action where relevant.
Application DB role may INSERT audit events and SELECT authorized records; no UPDATE/DELETE privilege for audit tables.
Time/tenant partitioning permitted for scale, but event IDs/order, retention and search remain consistent.
acceptance_intent: Partition maintenance cannot erase retained events.

required_behavior: Regulated aggregate event streams include previous event hash/current event hash using canonical event representation.
Periodically create signed integrity manifest/Merkle-style root or equivalent over audit ranges and store in immutable-capable storage.
Scheduled process verifies chain/checkpoint consistency and alarms on mismatch/missing ranges.
DBA/cloud-admin access and extraordinary actions are monitored through independent infrastructure/security logs and controlled procedures.
Authorized QA/auditor can filter by record, batch, user, event type, field, time, site, signature, source and reason.
If customer procedure requires documented audit-trail review, create separate review record/signature without changing the underlying audit events.
Generate human-readable and structured audit export tied to exact record/export manifest and integrity checks.
Audit retained at least as long as associated regulated record policy; archival retains search/retrieval and integrity evidence.
Retention engine can suspend disposal/archive transitions for held records/events.
Operational logs may redact sensitive values, but authorized GxP audit/evidence must preserve required content/meaning. Secrets must never be captured.
Migrated records include provenance/migration events and source checksums without pretending migrated events occurred natively.
Policy-denied/replay/attack events may be sent to security ledger/SIEM; only failed actions with GxP significance need GxP audit according to risk/policy.
Persist per-aggregate monotonic version/sequence and database commit order metadata where needed; source timestamp does not control authoritative order.
Restore procedure verifies audit record counts, hash checkpoints, references and signature linkage.
Application users and admins cannot delete audit events via normal UI/API. Retention disposal, if ever permitted, is a separately controlled archival process based on applicable policy.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Every released master, specification, controlled document snapshot and regulated final record receives immutable vault version ID.
acceptance_intent: Released content cannot be edited in place.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Vault stores canonical structured representation sufficient to reproduce content/meaning independent of mutable Frappe master.
acceptance_intent: Changing Frappe draft does not change vault object.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Calculate and store algorithm + digest over canonical representation and evidence manifest.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Store object type, business ID, version, status, effective dates, release reason, authors/approvers/signatures and software/schema versions.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Link immutable file/evidence IDs, hashes, media types and versions used by released object.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: At batch/device work issuance, freeze exact released recipe/specification/material/equipment/rule references required for that execution.
acceptance_intent: Later master change cannot rewrite active/history.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Snapshot captures exact IDs/versions/hashes of dependent released objects rather than only business names.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Released versions have controlled effective-from/effective-to/obsolete lifecycle; selection engine prevents unauthorized obsolete/future use.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: New approved version supersedes prior for future use but never deletes prior version or its historical references.
acceptance_intent: Old batches still resolve old version.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Corrections to regulated completed/released records create amendment/superseding version referencing original, reason, authority, signatures and changed fields.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Policy defines which record states/types permit correction, who may initiate/approve, and whether downstream impact assessment is required.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Any attempt to overwrite a vault object/version through application API is rejected.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Where a record must be voided/cancelled, retain original and add controlled status/event/reason rather than physical deletion.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Signatures reference exact vault version/hash or pre-commit canonical target that becomes exact resulting version.
acceptance_intent: Signature cannot float to new content.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Version creation/release/supersession/correction is represented in Audit Ledger.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Authorized user can retrieve any historical version plus relationships, signatures, audit and evidence manifest.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Export service can regenerate human-readable representation from stored authoritative version using controlled renderer/version or preserve signed release export.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Older canonical schema versions remain readable. Migrations never rewrite historical semantic content without controlled migration provenance.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Each object gets retention class based on profile/record type/customer policy; no normal application deletion.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Hold prevents disposal/archival transitions and is itself controlled/audited.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Move old vault objects/evidence to archival storage only if integrity, retrieval and meaning are preserved.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Released file packages/checkpoints may use object-storage retention lock/WORM where deployment supports it.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Use immutable internal version IDs plus human/business version labels; never rely only on editable semantic label.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Evidence objects may be deduplicated by digest while preserving record-specific manifest references and retention.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: DDCP snapshot can bind exact drug constituent version, device constituent version, compatibility version and final assembly/release rules.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Imported historical versions are flagged migrated, with source system, source ID, extraction checksum and migration batch.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Backup restore checks version counts, hashes, evidence manifests, signatures and audit relationships.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Draft authorship access does not imply released-vault write access; runtime exposes read plus controlled release/correction commands only.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Foreign references to released version use immutable identifiers and DB constraints/service validation; no dangling reference on normal operation.

module_title: Record Version Vault, Locking, Amendment & Controlled Correction
required_behavior: Final release/closure creates or references a complete immutable record package suitable for regulatory export and long-term retrieval.
Each user has immutable internal subject mapping to enterprise identity; shared regulated accounts prohibited.
acceptance_intent: Two users cannot share signing identity.

required_behavior: Support OIDC/SAML through Keycloak-compatible boundary; customer Entra/Okta/AD or equivalent may be source.
On-prem deployments may use controlled local Keycloak identity where customer SSO unavailable, subject to equivalent policies.
Provision, activate, suspend, disable, terminate and retain historical identity metadata.
Reference roles grouped by Production, QA, QC, Warehouse, Procurement, Engineering, QMS, IT and Auditor.
acceptance_intent: Role names configurable but permissions controlled.

required_behavior: Permissions are action/resource based, not merely screen access: view, create-draft, execute, verify, approve, release, correct, administer, export, etc.
Identity cannot access another customer environment/data.
User access can be limited to site, building, area/room/line and function where required.
Authorization may restrict user to product family, process type or specialized operation.
Model qualifications such as dispensing, sterile-area, aseptic operation, QA release, equipment use and specialized testing.
Required training/SOP curriculum status can be evaluated before execution/signing.
User may require equipment-specific or class qualification before operating/verifying.
Only users with active electronic-signature entitlement and verified identity status may complete regulated signature challenges.
Support performer != verifier, author != approver, independent QA release, and configurable incompatible role/action combinations.
SoD evaluates record history, not only static role membership; e.g. user who performed step cannot verify same step.
Tasks/approvals may be reassigned/delegated under controlled workflow, but electronic signature is never delegated.
Time-limited authorization has reason, scope, start/end, approver and audit; auto-expires.
Emergency access is explicitly invoked, MFA-protected, time-limited, reason-coded, heavily audited and independently reviewed.
Application admin, Security admin, Identity admin, DB admin and infrastructure admin remain separate from product release authority.
Support access requires customer-approved/time-limited identity, scoped permissions and logging; no shared vendor root account.
Non-human identities have owner, purpose, scopes, credential/certificate lifecycle, rotation and no human signature capability.
Edge/instruments use registered non-human device identities/certificates separate from service/human users.
Configurable idle/absolute timeout, reauthentication rules and session revocation. Regulated signature still uses fresh step-up.
MFA required for privileged access and configured enterprise policies; signature authentication follows Document 04 assurance.
acceptance_intent: Privileged account cannot use password-only baseline.

required_behavior: High-risk role/entitlement assignment uses controlled approval and audit; assignment effective dates supported.
Periodic report/review of active users, roles, sites, qualifications, service accounts and privileged access.
Identity changes synchronize through IdP/manual process while preserving immutable historical actor IDs.
Authorization response contains allow/deny, policy version, evaluated subject/resource/action and reason codes.
New users/service accounts have no regulated privileges until explicitly assigned.
Frappe permissions improve UX but GxP Policy Service independently enforces every authoritative regulated action.
Any permitted emergency qualification override requires dedicated policy, reason, authorized signer and quality-event/audit linkage.
User/account deletion is avoided where history is required; deactivated identity remains referencable for old records/signatures.
Every GxP-critical rule/formula has stable ID, type, semantic version, status, scope and owner.
Draft → Review → Approved/Released → Effective → Superseded/Retired. Released version immutable.
Rule version has effective-from/to and profile/site/product applicability; execution snapshots exact eligible version.
Same inputs + same released rule version produce same result, independent of UI/server instance.
GxP formulas/rules use constrained DSL/AST/function catalogue; arbitrary Python/JavaScript/SQL/network/file execution prohibited.
Inputs define data type, unit, required/optional, precision, acceptable null behavior and source.
Outputs define result type, unit, precision, status/reason codes and downstream action.
Use canonical UOM IDs and validated conversions; dimensional incompatibility rejected.
acceptance_intent: kg cannot be silently compared to L.

required_behavior: Use deterministic decimal arithmetic for regulated calculations; avoid binary floating-point where it could alter results.
Formula defines rounding mode, stage and decimal places/significant figures.
Support inclusive/exclusive min/max, target/tolerance, enumerations, ranges and conditional limits.
Material, equipment, operator, area, recipe and constituent eligibility rules evaluate before relevant action.
Define prerequisite steps, parallel joins, conditional branches, hold points and permitted progression.
Determine required signature meaning, signer role/qualification, independence and count/order.
Out-of-limit, expired status, manual override, timing breach, environment excursion or missing evidence can generate configured exception/hold.
Aggregate required completion/QC/QMS/reconciliation/signature/equipment/environment evidence into release eligibility result with blockers.
Support theoretical/actual/stage yield and percentage according to released formula, input sources, verification policy and rounding.
Support controlled potency correction with exact assay source/version, formula, units and precision.
Issued/dispensed/consumed/returned/rejected/destroyed quantities reconcile according to released rule/tolerance.
Support process hold times, expiry/retest, calibration due, training expiry, timer limits and environmental windows using authoritative time.
Every evaluation returns rule ID/version, inputs/reference IDs, outcome, reason codes and relevant calculated values.
Persist critical evaluation result/reference with regulated mutation/audit; avoid relying on recomputation under a newer rule.
Authorized users can simulate draft rules against test/historical sanitized data without affecting regulated state.
Each released critical rule includes approved positive, boundary, negative and error test vectors.
Critical formulas can require independent reviewer approval/test evidence before release.
acceptance_intent: Formula author cannot self-approve if policy says no.

required_behavior: Changing rule/formula triggers impact assessment for products, recipes, batches, tests, validation and customer configuration.
Batch/record snapshots reference exact rule/calculation versions required for execution.
acceptance_intent: Mid-batch rule change does not alter history.

required_behavior: LIMS/ERP/Edge values are validated against source mapping, unit, schema and quality before rule evaluation.
Rule defines explicit behavior: fail, hold, not-applicable or exception; never silently substitute default for critical missing data unless released rule permits.
Divide-by-zero, invalid logarithm/range, overflow, unit mismatch or invalid enum produce controlled failure with no fabricated result.
Record engine/runtime version separately from business rule version; engine upgrade requires regression.
acceptance_intent: Same rule under new engine validated.

required_behavior: Caching compiled rules is allowed only if cache key includes immutable rule version and tenant/profile; cache cannot alter deterministic outcome.

Create controlled product identity with immutable internal ID, business code, marketed/internal names, lifecycle state, product family, dosage/device form, strength/configuration, manufacturing profile, and site applicability.
acceptance_intent: Product can be uniquely referenced across recipes, batches, QC, genealogy and release.

required_behavior: Support Draft, Under Review, Approved/Released, Effective, Suspended, Obsolete, Superseded. Released product versions are immutable.
acceptance_intent: Obsolete/suspended product cannot start new production unless controlled exception policy permits.

required_behavior: Product changes create a new version with effective dating and Vault release; historical batches remain linked to prior version.
A DDCP product may contain Drug, Device, Biologic, HCT/P or Other constituent types; V1 actively supports Drug + Device and structurally supports later profiles.
acceptance_intent: Combination product is not represented as two unrelated masters.

required_behavior: Record primary/secondary constituent role, manufacturer/site source, business identity, exact version, lot/serial strategy and regulated handoff requirements.
Support Single Entity, Co-Packaged and Cross-Labeled/Other relationship metadata as controlled product attributes; exact regulatory applicability remains customer/regulatory decision.
acceptance_intent: Workflow can distinguish product relationship type.

required_behavior: Store customer-approved PMOA/lead-center/regulatory-context reference without software deciding PMOA.
acceptance_intent: Product does not infer regulatory classification.

required_behavior: Store customer-approved compliance approach/profile reference and applicable supplementary control set.
Assign one or more controlled manufacturing profiles: Injectable DDCP, Inhalation DDCP, Drug-Eluting/Coated Device, Device, Pharma, future extensions.
acceptance_intent: Recipe authoring can inherit valid process capabilities.

required_behavior: Flag whether sterile/aseptic controls apply and reference released sterile-process profile rather than free-text setting.
acceptance_intent: Sterile-required product cannot use non-sterile recipe path.

required_behavior: Configure finished lot, device lot, unit serial, combination-product serial, or hybrid genealogy strategy.
Configure UDI requirement, issuing-agency metadata, DI rules, production-identifier sources and packaging-level requirements where applicable.
Configure drug batch/lot identification and whether final product shares or differs from drug-constituent batch identity.
Represent drug strength/concentration using structured quantity + UOM and product-specific calculation metadata.
Represent device model/configuration/version and compatible drug constituent constraints.
acceptance_intent: Wrong device configuration cannot be paired.

required_behavior: Release controlled compatibility versions specifying allowed exact drug/device constituent combinations and critical interface constraints.
Reference released packaging hierarchy/configuration and label profile by product/version.
acceptance_intent: Packaging module uses exact approved configuration.

required_behavior: Reference released expiration/stability policy; product master does not hard-code computed expiration logic.
Reference structured storage/environment requirements and acceptable ranges.
acceptance_intent: Warehouse and batch rules can evaluate conditions.

required_behavior: Reference approved material/component structures; material specification versions remain separate controlled objects.
acceptance_intent: Product version does not duplicate mutable material specs.

required_behavior: Reference released finished/in-process/device test specifications and sampling profiles.
Reference allowed equipment/process classes and special validation requirements.
Product version has approved manufacturing/packaging/release sites and optional contract-manufacturing relationships.
Critical regulatory profile fields store source/decision reference, approver and effective version.
acceptance_intent: Audit can show basis of configuration.

required_behavior: Changing regulated product attributes triggers impact assessment for recipes, specs, labels, QC, validation, inventory, open batches and genealogy.
Allow draft clone from approved family/template, but cloned product receives new identity and requires full review/release.
Search by code, name, constituent type, manufacturing profile, site, lifecycle, UDI DI, device model, strength.
Maintain external-system IDs for ERP/LIMS/label systems without using external ID as internal primary key.
acceptance_intent: ERP mappings do not contaminate domain identity.

required_behavior: Quality may suspend future issue with reason/signature while preserving active/in-process batch policy separately.
acceptance_intent: Suspension does not rewrite past batches.

required_behavior: Produce human-readable product/profile/version report with constituents, applicability, approved sites, labels/spec references and release signatures.
acceptance_intent: Controlled master can be reviewed externally.

required_behavior: Before product release, validate mandatory attributes based on active manufacturing/regulatory profile.
Unsupported specialist context (e.g. biologic-specific or unsupported implantable/connected-device profile) fails closed unless corresponding profile package is approved.

Use pinned supported Python/Frappe, Node.js LTS/TypeScript and SQL versions defined by release toolchain; never code against floating latest.
Enable strict TypeScript with noUncheckedIndexedAccess/exactOptionalPropertyTypes or documented equivalent; any requires narrow justified exception.
Public Python services/functions use type hints; data structures use typed models/dataclasses/Pydantic-style validation as architecture permits.
Use domain-specific names; avoid vague manager/helper/util names for regulated concepts.
Split modules by cohesive responsibility; avoid god classes/services and cross-domain utility dumping grounds.
Public/domain functions declare typed inputs/outputs, errors and side effects; hidden DB/network behavior prohibited.
Calculations/rules/state-transition logic kept deterministic and independently testable where feasible.
Use Decimal/NUMERIC-compatible types for regulated values; binary floating point prohibited for regulated calculations unless raw measurement semantics require it.
Quantities carry explicit UOM and conversion provenance; unitless magic numbers prohibited.
Persist UTC timestamptz/timezone-aware datetimes; naive datetime prohibited in regulated code.
Use stable immutable IDs; external/business IDs are data, not DB ownership keys.
Use typed/stable domain error codes; do not branch application logic on exception message strings.
Catch only errors that can be handled; preserve cause/correlation; silent catch prohibited.
Structured logs use correlation/tenant/site/service/operation fields; secrets and unnecessary PII/GxP payloads redacted.
Comments explain why/invariant/regulatory reasoning, not restate obvious code; TODOs require issue/spec reference.
